newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs close lower, pork bellies mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs close lower, pork bellies mostly higher.

text.p: Expectations of weakening cash hog prices weighed on CME hog futures, which closed lower and near the day's lows, traders said. Pork bellies ended mostly higher after rallying following the expiration of August.

Packers were seen lowering bids for cash hogs after paying higher prices Tuesday and generally obtaining adequate supplies. A weak tone to cash pork prices will cut into packer margins and trim bids for hogs, they said.

USDA reported a weak undertone to wholesale pork prices at midday Tuesday, with hams quoted steady to $1.00 per cwt lower, bellies steady and trimmings lower. The news followed USDA reports Monday that pork cut-out values slid $0.18 to $0.27 per cwt.
"The (poor) packer margins have made them reluctant to aggressively buy hogs," said Karl Skold, Director of Research for Frontier Risk Management.
Hog futures closed 0.850 cent a lb lower to 0.050 higher with only distant December up and October off most at 53.800 cents.
But Skold did not look for an extended skid in futures as they already hold a discount.
Rand Financials notably sold October late while locals pressured December. Lind-Waldock and R.J. O'Brien bought December, pit sources said.
"Seasonally, we do get a break right in through here but the futures have a lot of that factored in already. I think (price) breaks below these levels will be bought," he said.

In hog options, ADM Investor Services bought the December 54 straddle while Lind-Waldock bought 70 to 74 February puts early. Volatility was softer in October and firm in back months, pit sources added.

Next year pork belly contracts rallied after the limit down expiration of August and finished 1.000 to 0.300 cent higher with February up 0.800 at 84.050 cents a lb. August was offered limit down from the start and at the noon expiration, settled at 88.250 cents.
Bearish sentiment from the August break was relieved and back months rallied on an oversold condition, traders said.
February and other 1997 contracts will now trade mostly technical until the new storage season starts later in the year, they said.
Prudential Securities bought after the August expiration and sparked a local short covering rally, traders said.
FIMAT, Merrill Lynch and Rand Financials had sold February early while E.D.& F. Man and Prudential bought on the setback, pit sources said.

After the close the CME reported net-out pork belly movement from warehouses outside Chicago last week of 0.247 million lbs, the low end of early estimates which ranged out 0.2 million to 2.0 million lbs.
